# Audit report: MEDIUM CHANGELOG misfiling fix

## Verdict: APPROVED

## What I verified (independent, against real artifacts)

**Substance (the actual user-facing value).** I reconstructed the pre-fix file from `HEAD~1` (1673 lines) and diffed against the new CHANGELOG.md (1844 lines):

- **Old state confirmed broken**: 16 headers only; 12 bullets misfiled under `## [Unreleased]` (warden v0.113.3, v0.113.47–50, v0.113.46 + phantom-incident bullet, v0.113.45/44/43/35, and the v0.113.7 pack-too-large bullet); the v0.112.15–19 bullets misfiled under `[0.113.7]`; header block at old lines 103–123 out of order (`[0.112.12]` → `[0.112.14]` → `[0.112.13]` → `[0.112.11]`).
- **New state correct**: 51 headers (50 versioned + empty `[Unreleased]` placeholder); strictly descending by numeric version across all 50 (my own check, not the executor's); old out-of-order block now `[0.112.14]` → `[0.112.13]` → `[0.112.12]` (empty, correctly) → `[0.112.11]`.
- **Zero content loss**: 195 bullet first-lines (executor said 194 — my regex includes an indented sub-bullet; immaterial) are **multiset-identical** old vs. new. Every bullet is accounted for in exactly one section; `[Unreleased]` holds zero bullets.
- **Routing correct**: automated check — for every single-bullet section, the version in the bullet's first line matches the header version. Zero mismatches.
- **Body preservation**: the pre-existing `[0.112.14]`→`[0.1.0]` region diff shows **only blank-line insertions** — no content line moved or altered, and the 121-bullet `[0.112.5]` aggregate section is untouched.
- **Finding-specific placements verified**: `[0.113.7]` holds clippy (### Added) + pack-too-large (### Fixed); `[0.113.46]` holds v0.113.46 + phantom bullet (dated 2026-08-08, matching the incident date); `[0.113.3] - 2026-08-09` holds the warden bullet; `[0.112.15]/[0.112.16]` hold their own bullets (previously stranded under `[0.113.7]`).

## Verification contract — evidence

$ git log -1 --format='%H%n%an <%ae>%n%s'

$ git show --stat HEAD | tail -3
 CHANGELOG.md | 179 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 175 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
$ git config user.name && git config user.email

dracsharp@gmail.com

Item: "this finding's box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md is checked ("- [x] … — fixed in <commit>")"
Output:
$ sed -n '35p' .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: parent CHANGELOG misfiles shipped releases under `## [Unreleased]` (v0.113.47-50, warden v0.113.3/0.3.1) while the last closed header is `[0.113.7] - 2026-07-28` — ~40 releases (0.113.8→0.113.50) never got closed headers; headers also out of order around lines 103-123 (`[0.112.12]` → `[0.112.14]` → `[0.112.13]` → `[0.112.11]`…). Entries exist and are accurate, just not filed under release headers (CHANGELOG.md:8-28) — fixed in 519cea42d
</evidence>

## Notes (non-blocking)

- The findings.md checkmark is uncommitted working-tree state (`M .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md`), disclosed by the executor; the contract requires the box *checked*, which it is, and the fix itself is committed at HEAD. The daemon auto-commits `.pi-glla` state as normal.
- The `[0.113.3] - 2026-08-09` header (warden release) is dated after `[0.113.7] - 2026-07-28`; that reflects the bullet's own release date and the independent warden version line — semantically correct, and no pre-existing `[0.113.3]` header was clobbered (old file had none).
- Releases with no changelog entries (e.g., 0.113.8–0.113.34) correctly get no headers — the objective was to stop *entries* from being misfiled, and every entry is now under a correctly-versioned closed header.

<approved/>
